title: Do Bulls Hate Red?

x.en: Bulls get angry at the color red.

o.en: Bulls notice movement, not color.

why.en: It's the movement, not the colour.
why.ko: 색이 아니라 움직임이야.

title: Does Swallowed Gum Stay for 7 Years?

x.en: Swallowed gum stays in your tummy for seven years.
x.ko: 삼킨 껌은 배 속에 7년 동안 남는다.

o.en: Swallowed gum passes in a few days.
o.ko: 삼킨 껌은 며칠이면 몸 밖으로 나온다.

why.en: Gum passes in a few days. But don't swallow it!
why.ko: 껌은 며칠이면 지나가. 그래도 삼키지는 마!

title: Can You See the Great Wall From Space?

x.en: You can easily see the Great Wall from space.

o.en: The Great Wall is very hard to see from space.

why.en: Long is not the same as easy to see.
why.ko: 길다고 잘 보이는 건 아니야.

title: Does Lightning Never Strike Twice?

x.en: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
x.ko: 번개는 같은 곳에 두 번 치지 않는다.

o.en: Lightning can strike the same place again and again.
o.ko: 번개는 같은 곳에 여러 번 칠 수 있다.

why.en: When thunder roars, go indoors!
why.ko: 천둥이 울리면, 안으로!

title: Do We Only Use 10% of Our Brain?

x.en: We only use ten percent of our brain.

o.en: We use all of our brain, just not all at once.
o.ko: 우리는 뇌를 다 쓴다. 한꺼번에가 아닐 뿐.

why.en: You use all of your brain, just not all at once.
why.ko: 뇌는 다 써. 한꺼번에가 아닐 뿐.

title: Are Bats Blind?

x.en: Bats are blind.

o.en: Bats can see.

why.en: Bats can see, and many can hear their way in the dark.
why.ko: 박쥐는 볼 수 있고, 많은 박쥐는 어둠 속에서 소리로 길을 찾아.

title: Do Carrots Help You See in the Dark?

x.en: Carrots let you see in the dark.

o.en: Carrots help healthy eyes, but they are not night vision.
o.ko: 당근은 눈 건강을 돕지만 밤눈 초능력은 아니다.

why.en: Carrots help healthy eyes, but they are not night vision.
why.ko: 당근은 건강한 눈을 돕지만, 밤눈 초능력은 아니야.

title: Do Ostriches Hide Their Heads in the Sand?

x.en: Ostriches hide their heads in the sand.

o.en: Ostriches run fast when they are in danger.

why.en: Ostriches don't hide their heads. They run!
why.ko: 타조는 머리를 숨기지 않아. 달려!

title: Will a Mother Bird Leave If You Touch Her Baby?

x.en: A mother bird leaves if you touch her baby.
x.ko: 아기 새를 만지면 엄마 새가 떠난다.

o.en: A mother bird won't leave just because you touched her baby.
o.ko: 아기 새를 만졌다고 엄마 새가 떠나지는 않는다.

why.en: Mom won't leave because of your touch. But look, don't touch!
why.ko: 손을 댔다고 엄마 새가 떠나진 않아. 그래도 보기만 해!

title: Does Sugar Make Kids Go Wild?

x.en: Sugar makes kids go wild.

o.en: Parties make kids excited, not sugar.
o.ko: 아이들을 들뜨게 하는 건 설탕이 아니라 파티다.

why.en: It's the party, not the sugar!
why.ko: 설탕이 아니라 파티야!

title: Do Camels Store Water in Their Humps?

x.en: A camel stores water in its hump.

o.en: A camel's hump is full of fat.

why.en: A camel's hump is full of fat, not water!
why.ko: 낙타 혹에는 물이 아니라 지방이 가득해!

title: Do Goldfish Really Have a Three-Second Memory?

x.en: A goldfish only remembers for three seconds.

o.en: A goldfish can remember for months.
o.ko: 금붕어는 몇 달 동안 기억할 수 있다.

why.en: A goldfish can remember for months, not seconds!
why.ko: 금붕어는 몇 초가 아니라 몇 달을 기억해!

title: Why Do Chameleons Really Change Color?

x.en: Chameleons change color to copy what's behind them.
x.ko: 카멜레온은 뒤 배경을 따라 색을 바꾼다.

o.en: Chameleons change color to send messages.

why.en: A chameleon sends messages with color. It doesn't copy!
why.ko: 카멜레온은 색으로 메시지를 보내. 따라 하는 게 아니야!

title: Does Cracking Your Knuckles Make Your Fingers Fat?

x.en: Cracking your knuckles makes your fingers fat.

o.en: Cracking your knuckles won't make your fingers fat.

why.en: That pop isn't your bones, and it won't make fat fingers!
why.ko: 그 소리는 뼈가 아니고, 손가락도 굵어지지 않아!

title: Is the Five-Second Rule Real?

x.en: Food is safe if you pick it up in five seconds.

o.en: Germs can get on food right away.
o.ko: 세균은 떨어진 음식에 바로 붙을 수 있다.

why.en: Germs can't count to five!
why.ko: 세균은 5까지 세지 못해!

title: Is Your Blood Blue Inside Your Body?

x.en: Your blood is blue inside your body.

o.en: Your blood is always red.

why.en: Your blood is always red. Light makes veins look blue!
why.ko: 피는 언제나 빨강이야. 빛 때문에 정맥이 파랗게 보여!

title: Is Summer Hot Because Earth Is Closer to the Sun?

x.en: Summer is hot because Earth is closer to the Sun.
x.ko: 여름이 더운 건 지구가 해에 더 가까워서다.

o.en: Summer comes because Earth leans.

why.en: Remember the leaning globe? Earth really leans like that.
why.ko: 기울어진 지구본 기억나? 지구는 진짜로 저렇게 기울어 있어.

title: Do Dogs Really See in Black and White?

x.en: Dogs see only in black and white.

o.en: Dogs see blue and yellow best.
o.ko: 개는 파랑과 노랑을 가장 잘 본다.

why.en: Dogs see blue and yellow best. Their world isn't just gray!
why.ko: 개는 파랑과 노랑을 가장 잘 봐. 세상이 회색만은 아니야!

title: Do Cats Always Land on Their Feet?

x.en: Cats always land on their feet.

o.en: Cats usually turn in the air, but not always.
o.ko: 고양이는 대개 공중에서 몸을 돌리지만 언제나는 아니다.

why.en: Cats usually turn in the air, but not always. And falls can still hurt them!
why.ko: 고양이는 대개 공중에서 돌지만 언제나는 아니야. 떨어지면 다칠 수도 있어!

title: Do We Lose Most of Our Body Heat Through Our Heads?

x.en: We lose most of our body heat through our heads.

o.en: Your head loses about one tenth of your heat.

why.en: Your head loses about one tenth of your heat. Still, wear your hat!
why.ko: 머리로 나가는 열은 약 10분의 1이야. 그래도 모자는 써!

title: Is the Sahara the Biggest Desert on Earth?

x.en: The Sahara is the biggest desert on Earth.

o.en: The biggest desert is cold Antarctica.

why.en: The biggest desert is cold Antarctica. The Sahara is the biggest hot one!
why.ko: 가장 큰 사막은 추운 남극이야. 사하라는 더운 사막 중 가장 커!

title: Do We Swallow Eight Spiders a Year in Our Sleep?

x.en: We swallow eight spiders a year in our sleep.
x.ko: 우리는 자면서 1년에 거미 여덟 마리를 삼킨다.

o.en: Spiders stay away from sleeping people.

why.en: Nobody has found proof of eight spiders a year. Spiders stay away from you!
why.ko: 1년에 여덟 마리라는 증거는 없어. 거미는 너를 피해 다녀!

title: Do Sunflowers Always Follow the Sun?

x.en: Sunflowers always follow the Sun.

o.en: Open sunflowers stop and face east.
o.ko: 활짝 핀 해바라기는 멈춰서 동쪽을 본다.

why.en: Young sunflowers follow the sun. Open ones stop and face east!
why.ko: 어린 해바라기는 해를 따라가. 꽃이 피면 멈추고 동쪽을 봐!

title: Do All Bees Die After They Sting?

x.en: All bees die after they sting.

o.en: Most bees don't die after they sting.
o.ko: 대부분의 벌은 쏘고 나서도 죽지 않는다.

why.en: A worker honey bee can die after a sting. Most other bees don't!
why.ko: 꿀벌 일벌은 쏘고 죽을 수 있지만, 다른 벌은 대부분 안 그래!

title: Do You Taste Sweet Only on the Tip of Your Tongue?

x.en: You taste sweet only on the tip of your tongue.

o.en: Taste buds all over your tongue sense every taste.
o.ko: 혀 곳곳의 맛봉오리가 모든 맛을 느낀다.

why.en: There's no sweet spot. Taste buds all over your tongue sense every taste!
why.ko: 단맛 자리는 따로 없어. 혀 곳곳의 맛봉오리가 모든 맛을 느껴!

title: Did Vikings Wear Horned Helmets?

x.en: Vikings wore horned helmets.

o.en: No Viking horned helmet has been found.
o.ko: 바이킹 뿔 투구는 발견된 적이 없다.

why.en: No Viking horned helmet has been found. The horns came from art and shows!
why.ko: 바이킹 뿔 투구는 발견된 적이 없어. 뿔은 그림과 공연에서 왔어!

title: Do Bananas Grow on Trees?

x.en: Bananas grow on trees.

o.en: A banana plant is a giant herb.

why.en: A banana plant is a giant herb, not a tree. Its trunk is rolled leaves!
why.ko: 바나나는 나무가 아니라 거대한 풀이야. 줄기는 말린 잎이고!

title: Is the Far Side of the Moon Always Dark?

x.en: The far side of the Moon is always dark.

o.en: The far side of the Moon gets sunlight, too.

why.en: The far side gets sunlight, too. We just can't see it from Earth!
why.ko: 뒷면도 햇빛을 받아. 지구에서 안 보일 뿐이야!

title: Can Owls Turn Their Heads All the Way Around?

x.en: Owls can turn their heads all the way around.
x.ko: 올빼미는 고개를 한 바퀴 다 돌릴 수 있다.

o.en: An owl can turn its head about 270 degrees.
o.ko: 올빼미는 고개를 약 270도 돌릴 수 있다.

why.en: An owl can turn its head about 270 degrees each way, but not a full circle!
why.ko: 올빼미는 양쪽으로 약 270도 돌리지만, 한 바퀴는 아니야!

title: Was Napoleon Really Short?

x.en: Napoleon was very short.

o.en: Napoleon was about average height for his time.

why.en: Napoleon was about average for his time. Old numbers and cartoons fooled us!
why.ko: 나폴레옹은 그 시대 평균쯤이었어. 옛 숫자와 만화에 속은 거야!

title: Do Mice Really Love Cheese?

x.en: Cheese is a mouse's favorite food.

o.en: Mice usually like grains and sweet foods better.
o.ko: 쥐는 대개 곡식과 단 먹이를 더 좋아한다.

why.en: A hungry mouse eats cheese, but mice usually like grains and sweet foods better!
why.ko: 배고픈 쥐는 치즈도 먹지만, 대개 곡식과 단 먹이를 더 좋아해!

title: Are Peanuts Really Nuts?

x.en: Peanuts are nuts that grow on trees.

o.en: Peanuts grow under the ground.

why.en: Peanuts are legumes. They grow under the ground, not on trees!
why.ko: 땅콩은 콩과 식물이야. 나무가 아니라 땅속에서 자라!

title: Do Diamonds Come From Coal?

x.en: Diamonds come from coal.

o.en: Most diamonds formed much deeper than coal.
o.ko: 다이아몬드는 대개 석탄보다 훨씬 깊은 곳에서 생겼다.

why.en: Diamonds and coal share carbon, but most diamonds formed deeper and much earlier!
why.ko: 다이아몬드와 석탄은 탄소를 나누지만, 다이아몬드는 대개 더 깊고 훨씬 일찍 생겼어!

title: Does Cold Air Give You a Cold?

x.en: Cold air alone gives you a cold.

o.en: Viruses give you colds.

why.en: Viruses give you colds. Cold air alone does not, but wear your coat!
why.ko: 감기는 바이러스 때문이야. 찬 공기만으로는 안 걸려. 그래도 외투는 입어!

title: Are Polar Bears Really White?

x.en: Polar bears have white skin.

o.en: Polar bears have black skin.

why.en: Polar bears have black skin, and their fur only looks white!
why.ko: 북극곰은 피부가 검고, 털은 하얗게 보일 뿐이야!

title: Is Glass Really a Slow Liquid?

x.en: Glass is a slow liquid.

o.en: Glass acts like a solid.

why.en: Glass acts like a solid. Old windows were made uneven, and they did not flow!
why.ko: 유리는 고체처럼 행동해. 옛 창은 고르지 않게 만들어졌을 뿐, 흘러내린 게 아니야!

title: Did Einstein Really Fail Math?

x.en: Einstein failed math.

o.en: Einstein never failed math.

why.en: Einstein never failed math. He missed one exam because of other subjects!
why.ko: 아인슈타인은 수학을 낙제한 적이 없어. 시험 하나를 다른 과목 때문에 놓쳤을 뿐이야!

title: Does Water Spin the Other Way in Australia?

x.en: Sink water always spins the other way in Australia.
x.ko: 호주에서는 세면대 물이 언제나 반대로 돈다.

o.en: Sink water spins because of the sink's shape.
o.ko: 세면대 물은 세면대 모양 때문에 돈다.

why.en: The Earth's turn bends giant storms, but your sink spins because of its shape and its water!
why.ko: 지구의 회전은 거대한 폭풍을 휘게 하지만, 세면대 물은 모양과 물살 때문에 돌아!

title: Does a Cut Worm Become Two Worms?

x.en: A cut worm becomes two worms.

o.en: A cut worm does not become two worms.
o.ko: 지렁이를 잘라도 두 마리가 되지 않는다.

why.en: A cut worm does not become two worms. At best, the head half regrows a tail!
why.ko: 지렁이를 잘라도 두 마리가 되지 않아. 잘해야 머리 쪽이 꼬리를 다시 키울 뿐이야!

title: Does Shaving Make Hair Grow Back Thicker?

x.en: Shaving makes hair grow back thicker.

o.en: Shaving does not change your hair.

why.en: Shaving does not change your hair. It only leaves a blunt tip!
why.ko: 면도는 털을 바꾸지 않아. 끝을 뭉툭하게 남길 뿐이야!

title: Did Marie Antoinette Say Let Them Eat Cake?

x.en: Marie Antoinette said, "Let them eat cake."

o.en: Nobody has found proof that Marie Antoinette said it.
o.ko: 마리 앙투아네트가 그 말을 했다는 증거는 없다.

why.en: Nobody has found proof that she said it. The story is a rumor!
why.ko: 그가 말했다는 증거는 없어. 그 이야기는 소문이야!

title: Are Fortune Cookies Really From China?

x.en: Fortune cookies come from China.

o.en: Fortune cookies likely began in Japan.
o.ko: 포춘 쿠키는 일본에서 시작된 것으로 보인다.

why.en: Fortune cookies likely began in Japan and grew up in America!
why.ko: 포춘 쿠키는 일본에서 시작해 미국에서 자란 것으로 보여!

title: Is There No Gravity in Space?

x.en: There is no gravity in space.

o.en: There is gravity in space.

why.en: There is gravity in space. Astronauts float because they are falling!
why.ko: 우주에도 중력이 있어. 비행사들은 떨어지고 있어서 떠 있는 거야!

title: Is the Sun Really Yellow?

x.en: The Sun is yellow.

o.en: Sunlight is white.

why.en: Sunlight is white. The air makes it look yellow!
why.ko: 햇빛은 흰빛이야. 공기 때문에 노랗게 보여!

title: Do Watermelon Seeds Grow in Your Tummy?

x.en: Watermelon seeds grow in your tummy.

o.en: A seed can't grow in your tummy.

why.en: A seed can't grow in your tummy. It just passes through!
why.ko: 씨는 배 속에서 자라지 못해. 그냥 지나갈 뿐이야!

title: Do Penguins Live at the North Pole?

x.en: Penguins live at the North Pole.

o.en: Wild penguins live in the south.

why.en: Wild penguins live in the south, not at the North Pole!
why.ko: 야생 펭귄은 남쪽에 살아. 북극이 아니야!

title: Did People Think the Earth Was Flat?

x.en: In Columbus's time, people thought the Earth was flat.
x.ko: 콜럼버스 시대 사람들은 지구가 평평하다고 생각했다.

o.en: In Columbus's time, people knew the Earth was round.
o.ko: 콜럼버스 시대 사람들은 지구가 둥근 걸 알았다.

why.en: In Columbus's time, people knew the Earth was round. They argued about its size!
why.ko: 콜럼버스 시대 사람들은 지구가 둥근 걸 알았어. 다툰 건 크기였어!

title: Do We Have Only Five Senses?

x.en: We have only five senses.

o.en: We have more than five senses.

why.en: We have more than five senses, like balance and knowing where your body is!
why.ko: 우리 감각은 다섯 개보다 많아. 균형 감각, 몸의 위치 감각처럼!

title: Is a Tomato a Vegetable?

x.en: In science, a tomato is a vegetable.

o.en: In science, a tomato is a fruit.

why.en: In science, a tomato is a fruit. In the kitchen, we use it like a vegetable!
why.ko: 과학에서 토마토는 열매야. 부엌에서는 채소처럼 쓰지!

title: Do Toads Give You Warts?

x.en: Touching a toad gives you warts.

o.en: Toads don't give you warts.

why.en: Toads don't give you warts. But always wash your hands after touching one!
why.ko: 두꺼비는 사마귀를 옮기지 않아. 그래도 만진 뒤엔 꼭 손을 씻어!

title: Do Lemmings Jump Off Cliffs?

x.en: Lemmings jump off cliffs together.

o.en: Lemmings move to find food and space.

why.en: Lemmings don't jump off cliffs together. They move to find food and space!
why.ko: 레밍은 다 같이 절벽에서 뛰어내리지 않아. 먹이와 자리를 찾아 떠나는 거야!

title: Can Porcupines Shoot Their Quills?

x.en: Porcupines can shoot their quills.

o.en: A porcupine's quills come off when you touch them.

why.en: Porcupines can't shoot their quills. The quills come off when you touch them!
why.ko: 호저는 가시를 쏘지 못해. 가시는 닿을 때 빠지는 거야!

title: Are Elephants Scared of Mice?

x.en: Elephants are scared of mice.

o.en: Elephants avoid bees.

why.en: Elephants aren't scared of mice. They don't like surprises, and they avoid bees!
why.ko: 코끼리는 쥐를 무서워하지 않아. 깜짝 놀라는 걸 싫어하고, 벌을 피해!

title: Is Everest the Tallest Mountain?

x.en: From bottom to top, Everest is the tallest mountain.
x.ko: 밑에서 꼭대기까지 재면 에베레스트가 가장 큰 산이다.

o.en: From bottom to top, Mauna Kea is taller than Everest.
o.ko: 밑에서 꼭대기까지 재면 마우나케아가 에베레스트보다 크다.

why.en: Everest has the highest top. But from bottom to top, Mauna Kea is taller!
why.ko: 에베레스트는 꼭대기가 가장 높아. 하지만 밑에서 꼭대기까지는 마우나케아가 더 커!

title: Can a Falling Coin Knock You Out?

x.en: A coin dropped from a tall building can knock you out.
x.ko: 높은 빌딩에서 떨어진 동전에 맞으면 기절한다.

o.en: Air slows a falling coin down.

why.en: Air slows a falling coin, so it won't knock you out. But never drop things from high places!
why.ko: 공기가 떨어지는 동전을 늦춰서 기절하지는 않아. 그래도 높은 곳에서 절대 떨어뜨리지 마!

title: Does a Duck's Quack Echo?

x.en: A duck's quack doesn't echo.
x.ko: 오리 꽥꽥 소리는 메아리가 울리지 않는다.

o.en: A duck's quack does echo.

why.en: A duck's quack does echo. It's just hard to hear!
why.ko: 오리 꽥꽥 소리도 메아리가 울려. 잘 안 들릴 뿐이야!

title: Does Reading in Dim Light Hurt Your Eyes?

x.en: Reading in dim light hurts your eyes forever.
x.ko: 어두운 데서 책을 읽으면 눈이 영영 나빠진다.

o.en: Dim light can make your eyes tired.

why.en: Dim light can make your eyes tired, but it doesn't hurt them forever!
why.ko: 어두우면 눈이 피곤할 수는 있지만, 영영 나빠지지는 않아!

title: Can You See the Moon in the Daytime?

x.en: You can only see the Moon at night.

o.en: You can see the Moon in the daytime, too.

why.en: You can see the Moon in the daytime too. Just look up!
why.ko: 달은 낮에도 보여. 위를 올려다보기만 해!

title: Do Dogs Sweat Through Their Tongues?

x.en: Dogs sweat through their tongues.

o.en: Dogs pant to cool down.

why.en: Dogs don't sweat through their tongues. They pant to cool down!
why.ko: 개는 혀로 땀을 흘리지 않아. 헐떡여서 더위를 식혀!

title: Are Raindrops Shaped Like Tears?

x.en: Raindrops are shaped like tears.

o.en: Small raindrops are round.

why.en: Small raindrops are round, and big ones look like buns. Not tears!
why.ko: 작은 빗방울은 둥글고, 큰 빗방울은 빵 모양이야. 눈물이 아니야!

title: Do Sharks Have to Keep Swimming?

x.en: All sharks must keep swimming or they die.
x.ko: 모든 상어는 계속 헤엄치지 않으면 죽는다.

o.en: Many sharks can rest.

why.en: Some sharks must keep swimming, but many sharks can rest!
why.ko: 계속 헤엄쳐야 하는 상어도 있지만, 많은 상어는 쉴 수 있어!

title: Do Elephants Drink Through Their Trunks?

x.en: Elephants drink water through their trunks like a straw.
x.ko: 코끼리는 코를 빨대처럼 써서 물을 마신다.

o.en: An elephant sprays water from its trunk into its mouth.
o.ko: 코끼리는 코에 담은 물을 입에 뿜어 넣는다.

why.en: An elephant fills its trunk with water, then sprays it into its mouth!
why.ko: 코끼리는 코에 물을 담았다가 입에 뿜어 넣어!

title: Do Fish Sleep?

x.en: Fish never sleep.

o.en: Fish do sleep, in their own way.

why.en: Fish do sleep, in their own way. Most keep their eyes open!
why.ko: 물고기도 나름대로 자. 대부분 눈을 뜬 채로!

title: Do Plants Eat Soil?

x.en: Plants eat soil.

o.en: Plants make their own food with sunlight.

why.en: Plants don't eat soil. They make their own food with sunlight!
why.ko: 식물은 흙을 먹지 않아. 햇빛으로 자기 양분을 만들어!

title: Do Butterflies Taste With Their Feet?

x.en: Butterflies can only taste with their mouths.

o.en: A butterfly can taste with its feet.
o.ko: 나비는 발로 맛을 볼 수 있다.

why.en: A butterfly can taste a flower with its feet!
why.ko: 나비는 발로 꽃 맛을 볼 수 있어!

title: Can a Turtle Crawl Out of Its Shell?

x.en: A turtle can crawl out of its shell.
x.ko: 거북은 등딱지에서 기어 나올 수 있다.

o.en: A turtle's shell is part of its body.

why.en: A turtle's shell is part of its body. It can never crawl out!
why.ko: 거북 등딱지는 몸의 한 부분이야. 절대 기어 나올 수 없어!

title: Is a Starfish a Fish?

x.en: A starfish is a fish.

o.en: A starfish is not a fish.

why.en: A starfish is not a fish. It's a sea star!
why.ko: 불가사리는 물고기가 아니야. 바다의 별이야!

title: Are Koalas Bears?

x.en: Koalas are bears.

o.en: A koala's baby grows in a pouch.

why.en: A koala is not a bear. Its baby grows in a pouch!
why.ko: 코알라는 곰이 아니야. 아기는 주머니에서 자라!

title: Are Snakes Slimy?

x.en: Snakes are slimy.

o.en: A snake's scales are dry and smooth.

why.en: Snakes are not slimy. Their scales are dry and smooth!
why.ko: 뱀은 미끈하지 않아. 비늘은 마르고 매끈해!

title: Do Giraffes Have More Neck Bones?

x.en: A giraffe has more neck bones than you.

o.en: A giraffe has seven neck bones, just like you.

why.en: A giraffe has seven neck bones, just like you!
why.ko: 기린 목뼈는 우리처럼 일곱 개야!

title: Do Rabbits Live on Carrots?

x.en: A rabbit's main food is carrots.

o.en: Rabbits eat mostly hay and grass.

why.en: Rabbits eat mostly hay and grass. Carrots are just a treat!
why.ko: 토끼는 거의 건초와 풀을 먹어. 당근은 간식일 뿐이야!
